data.name: Reading.CountsNote
data.value: A count is how long a long vowel is held: two is an ordinary long vowel, four and six are twice and three times as long. In writing, length is a repeated letter, but there are not as many letters as counts: two counts — two letters, four — three, five — four, six — five. The writing does not count harakat as letters: it puts the lengths in order, and each count looks different.

data.name: Reading.SwitchableNote
data.value: Rules with a switch can be left out: they do not change what other rules depend on. A rule switched off is read as in ordinary reading, everything else as in full tajweed. The Standard and Latin profiles do not write the ghunnah of ikhfa or the qalqalah echo: switching them off shows in the rule’s row and in your own profile, where they have a letter.
